extracted.intended_audience: Ethics reviewers for NeurIPS 2024 (and program committee members assigning ethics reviews)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for performing ethics reviews of NeurIPS submissions that have been flagged for potential ethical risks, including what to evaluate, how to communicate, and expected reviewer behavior and availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: areas of ethical risk to assess
rubrics_metrics.description: The role of ethics review is to assess NeurIPS submissions for risks in at least one of the following areas: Research involving human subjects; Data privacy, copyright, and consent; Data quality and representativeness; Safety and security; Discrimination, bias, and fairness; Deception and harassment; Environmental Impact; Human rights (including surveillance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assigned a paper, evaluate risks within these domains; an ethics review need only cover the areas flagged by primary reviewers but may identify additional areas. Use these categories as a checklist for potential harms and impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity of flagged ethical concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: When the primary review flags a paper, it indicates a claim that an ethical concern exists. Your role as an ethics reviewer is to validate or disprove this claim, focusing on the evaluation of the claim and providing a critical discussion supporting your evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus your review on whether the flagged concern is real and substantiated (e.g., safety/security misuse, deepfakes). It is perfectly acceptable to conclude that no ethical concern exists; provide clear reasoning either way. Provide critical discussion and evidence for your judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify unflagged ethical concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there any additional ethical concerns that were not flagged?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond validating the flagged issues, actively look for other ethical risks not raised by primary reviewers and call them out with justification and examples where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigation adequacy (authors' proposed mitigations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the authors suggest or implement mitigation strategies that sufficiently address the ethical risks? Note that a paper does not need to completely resolve the ethical risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether proposed mitigations are appropriate and sufficient. If mitigations are incomplete or lacking, recommend reasonable mitigation strategies the authors could consider. Be specific about what would make the mitigation adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation of additional mitigations
rubrics_metrics.description: As appropriate, reviewers are encouraged to suggest additional mitigation strategies that the authors could consider to alleviate the risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide practical, reasonable strategies (technical, procedural, documentation, release controls, disclaimers, etc.) and explain how they reduce risk. Frame suggestions constructively, indicating feasibility and residual risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer load and timing expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethics reviewers are asked to review up to 5 papers each and provide ethics reviews during specified review periods: July 15-26, 2024 (main track), July 26-August 6, 2024 (Datasets & Benchmarks track), with August 7-30, 2024 available for emergency/late reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sign up only if you can meet these windows. Participate asynchronously in follow-up discussions with authors and program committee during the author response period (August 2024). Inform ACs if you will be unavailable for extended stretches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability: communicate absences
rubrics_metrics.description: It's okay to be unavailable for part of the review process (e.g., on vacation for a few days). However, if you will be unavailable for a longer period, especially during crucial times (e.g., the discussion phase), please inform us and your ACs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively communicate availability constraints to area chairs to avoid assignment problems and ensure timely reviews and participation in discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and conflict-of-interest rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not discuss submissions assigned to you with other reviewers, ACs, or SACs without prior approval from your AC. Do not discuss your own submissions (i.e., those you are an author on) or submissions with which you have a conflict with other reviewers, ACs, and SACs. Keep papers assigned to you absolutely confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the corresponding AC as your primary point of contact for any permitted discussions. Follow conflict-of-interest policies strictly; breach of confidentiality is unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive reviews and neutral language
rubrics_metrics.description: Write thoughtful and constructive reviews. Ensure your reviews align with the NeurIPS code of conduct. Although the double-blind review process helps reduce discrimination, subtle discrimination can still occur and should be actively avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use neutral, constructive phrasing (example: replace 'Please have your submission proof-read by a native English speaker' with 'Please have your submission proof-read for English style and grammar issues'). Avoid ad hominem or culturally biased comments; focus on technical and ethical substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professionalism and engagement in discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Be professional, polite, and listen to other reviewers. Do not succumb to undue influence. Actively engage in the discussion phase for each of your assigned submissions, even if not specifically prompted by the AC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat colleagues and authors respectfully; provide clear, evidence-based arguments in discussions; participate to clarify ethics assessments and ensure the program committee has the context needed for decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoroughness and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: It is unfair to dismiss any submission without thoroughly reading it. Reflect on times when you received an unfair, unjustified, short, or dismissive review and strive not to be that reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the paper carefully before making ethics judgments; if citing existing work to justify comments, be precise and provide a complete citation. If you want authors to clarify something during the author response phase, articulate this clearly (e.g., 'I would like to see a discussion on risk X').

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review sensitivity (emotional/contextual awareness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bear in mind the positive and objective aspects, especially in ethics reviews, where the content itself could provoke emotionally charged responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain objectivity when evaluating ethically sensitive topics; avoid reactive language driven by emotional responses and focus on reasoned assessment of risks and mitigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural inclusiveness in ethics evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical concerns are sometimes deeply intertwined with personal lived experiences and cultural norms. We ask ethics reviewers to consider that paper submissions at NeurIPS come from all over the world, and encourage you to evaluate if the ethics concerns under review are sensitive to cultural context and may not be a worldwide issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider cultural context when judging harms and suggested mitigations; avoid assuming a single cultural perspective is universal. Explain when a concern may be culturally specific and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility and fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: With great power comes great responsibility! Take your role seriously and be fair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply standards consistently across submissions, avoid bias, and ensure your evaluation is proportionate to the evidence and the scope of the work.
